purpose: Teach: 熊野/小澤/杉田/菅原/豊島/志村/川原/清原

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが熊野詣でを毎年されてた
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to visit Kumano shrine every year.
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic opening. Soft voice, unhurried pace. Eyes distant with memory. Slight pause before the shrine name, as if seeing it again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、小澤征爾の演奏会に行かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: That's right — and you used to go see Ozawa Seiji conduct, remember dear?
lines.style: Warm, slightly teasing lilt. Quick and engaged, but with the affection of someone testing a shared memory. The 'dear' lands gently, conspiratorial.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが杉田玄白の解体新書を蔵書された
lines.en: When your father was young, he collected copies of Sugita Genpaku's anatomy texts.
lines.style: Quiet reverence in the voice. Slower delivery, almost scholarly. The titles are pronounced with care — he's proud of this memory, holding it carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、菅原道真の歴史小説を愛読されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Ah, and you used to read Sugawara no Michizane's novels all the time back then, didn't you dear?
lines.style: Bright, knowing smile in the voice. Slightly faster than before — she's enjoying herself now, gently redirecting. The 'didn't you dear' is playful nudge, not accusation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが豊島区池袋によく出かけられた
lines.en: When your father was young, he often went out to Toshima, to Ikebukuro.
lines.style: Slower, more reflective. A touch of fondness for the ordinary detail. Voice settles into the memory like settling into an old chair.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、志村けんのコントを毎週観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you watched Shimura Ken's comedy sketches every week, didn't you dear?
lines.style: Quick, delighted laugh underneath. Light and knowing. She's clearly enjoying this back-and-forth now, the rhythm of it. Warm close to the phrase.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが川原で写生をされた
lines.en: When your father was young, he used to sketch by the riverbank.
lines.style: Quietest yet. Almost to himself. The memory is tender and specific. Pause before 'riverbank' — he can almost see it. Trailing off slightly, letting the image linger.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、野球の清原和博選手を応援されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You used to cheer for Kiyohara Kazuhiro in baseball games, didn't you dear?
lines.style: Warm, intimate close. Voice draws in slightly, like she's speaking just to him. Genuine affection under the playfulness. Soft landing on the final phrase.
